label: rem:higgs-vacuum-residual-graviton
title: Graviton candidate 3: the symmetric square of the Higgs-vacuum residual
html:
Interpretive remark (physics reading, not a mathematical claim). The mass-endomorphism conjecture says that the graviton is "the residual of \Phi_{\rm mass} after subtracting the Higgs contribution". The vacuum-residual proposition gives one precise reading of that sentence at the level of idempotents. Read e = t^{-1}\varrho_\Phi\varrho_\Phi^{*} as the Higgs contribution on X = A^{(H)}, and r = \mathrm{id} - e as the residual. On the two-vacuum object X \otimes X, the residual of e \otimes e splits along the symmetry \beta_{X,X}. Its purely residual, symmetric summand P_{+} \circ (r \otimes r) is the graviton candidate (candidate 3): the symmetric part of (vacuum residual) \otimes (vacuum residual) on X \otimes X.

This is a choice of identification. It is not derived. By the "defined residual \neq derived decomposition" rule, r := \mathrm{id} - e is a definition. The proposition proves only that r, R = \mathrm{id} - e \otimes e and P_{\pm} \circ R are complementary idempotents. It does not prove that any of them is the graviton, and it does not prove that \Phi_{\rm mass} splits as "e-part plus r-part". That would need \Phi_{\rm mass} to commute with e, which is open.

What remains before "spin 2" could be claimed.

  1. A rotation action on X. The labels (\tfrac12, \tfrac12) in Table 1 are (j, y) for G = \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{U}(1)_Y: weak isospin and hypercharge. They are not (j_L, j_R) for a Lorentz or rotation group. So a spin label on P_{+}\circ(r \otimes r) first needs an \mathrm{SU}(2) that acts on X, fixes \varrho_\Phi, and is identified with spatial rotation. A candidate is the custodial diagonal of \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_R acting on the real 4-dimensional doublet. A text search of the corpus finds no custodial group; none is formalised.
  2. The residual must be spin 1, and the object matters. The spin-1 reading needs X to be the real four-dimensional doublet, with \operatorname{im} r the three directions orthogonal to the vacuum. Neither identification is made here. On the object the corpus actually names, X = A^{(H)} with \dim_q A^{(H)} = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_{A^{(H)}}) = [2]_q by (G-2) and \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{1}}) = 1, item 8 of the proposition gives \mathrm{tr}(r) = [2]_q - 1, which is 1 at q = 1: a residual of dimension one, not three. So the spin-2 reading is not available on A^{(H)} as (G-2) describes it.
  3. Removing the trace. \mathrm{Sym}^2(\text{spin }1) = \text{spin }2 \oplus \text{spin }0. Isolating spin 2 needs a further idempotent on P_{+}\circ(r\otimes r) that subtracts the trace part through the evaluation / coevaluation of \operatorname{im} r (a rigid / pivotal datum). No such idempotent is constructed here.
  4. Quantum dimensions. Item 8 of the proposition gives \mathrm{tr}(e_H) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{1}}) for any cyclic trace, so \mathrm{tr}(e_H) = 1 whenever the unit has trace 1. This is the value (G-4) states; the factor [2]_q belongs to \dim_q A^{(H)} in (G-2), not to the rank-one image of e_H.

No empirical quantity enters the proposition. The value t = v^2/m_e^2 in (G-3) plays no role: only t \neq 0 is used.
